name: Annual RMCP and Risk and Compliance Return filing kit for small law firms and other Schedule 1 accountable institutions
buyer: Small legal practices (Item 1) and other small Schedule 1 institutions such as credit providers and dealers in high-value goods
trigger: FIC Act s42 and s45C: an annual RMCP submission directive (October cut-offs; newly established institutions within 90 days) and the yearly Risk and Compliance Return (Directive 11 of 2026, due 30 Jun 2026). The LSSA draft guidance says a generic template does not equal compliance.
existing: Moonstone FICA Toolkit (templates), LSSA guidance, and consultants. The competitor search found no workflow software aimed at small institutions.
unchecked: Final or draft status of the RMCP submission directive (sources conflict) and exact items and dates; which Schedule 1 items are small-firm heavy; the FIC's own portal features; overlap with the estate agency candidate (same duty family, different buyers).

first_check.duty: FIC Act s42 RMCP and FIC Directive 12 (GG 55337, 4 Sep 2026, effective 7 Sep 2026). Annual RMCP submission via goAML: items 1 (legal practitioners), 2, 9 and 11 (non-bank credit providers) by 9 Oct each year; items 3, 14, 20 (high-value goods dealers), 21 and 22 by 31 Oct. New institutions file within 90 days of starting business, and amended RMCPs within 10 days of approval. Each board-approved RMCP is submitted once per Schedule 1 item registration. The RCR is a separate yearly return under Directive 11 (2026), filed in a different system. Non-compliance draws s45C administrative sanctions of up to R10m for natural persons and R50m for legal persons. Secondary sources give the exact item dates and agree with each other, but I did not read the gazette itself.
first_check.market: The FIC database had 55,262 registered institutions in 2024/25, up from 51,020 in 2023/24. The only sector split I found is from 2019/20, when attorneys were about 35% and estate agents about 24% of registrants. I found no current per-item figures for items 1, 11 or 20.
first_check.competitor: nCino KYC (formerly DocFox) markets a tested RMCP template, configuration against the firm's own RMCP, and an LSSA partnership with free onboarding for attorneys, but its core product is KYC/CDD. The Moonstone Compliance FICA Toolkit is a DIY RMCP template with a risk register and goAML registration help. The LSSA has published draft RMCP guidelines for free, and compliance consultants also serve this market. I found no dedicated RMCP-tailoring and filing workflow product for small institutions. The FIC's goAML portal only accepts uploads; it does not help write the RMCP.
first_check.reason: The duty is real and final. FIC Directive 12 (Gazette 55337, 4 Sep 2026, in force 7 Sep) requires items 1, 2, 9 and 11 to file their RMCP through goAML by 9 Oct each year, and items 3, 14, 20, 21 and 22 by 31 Oct. New institutions file within 90 days and amendments within 10 days. The RCR is a separate yearly return under Directive 11. Sanctions fall under s45C. I found no software that tailors and files the RMCP end to end. The nearest products are nCino KYC (DocFox: RMCP template, LSSA partnership, KYC-focused), the Moonstone DIY toolkit and consultants. The filing happens only once a year, the FIC discourages generic templates, and the first 9 Oct deadline is today, so recurring value is limited. A tailoring service that bundles the RCR could still sell to about 55k registrants.

challenge_check.killer: None found. The closest products are nCino KYC/DocFox (a KYC/CDD platform with an RMCP template and an LSSA partnership), the Moonstone FICA Toolkit (a R4,995 one-off DIY template), ClearComply (a deadline tracker from R99/month that does not build RMCPs) and consultants. The FIC's goAML only takes uploads.
challenge_check.reason: Directive 12 is now final (Gazette 55337, effective 7 Sep 2026). Items 1, 2, 9 and 11 must submit the board-approved RMCP via goAML by 9 Oct each year. Items 3, 14, 20, 21 and 22 must submit by 31 Oct. Revisions are due within 10 days of approval and new institutions within 90 days; there is no small-firm exemption. Three corrections to the claim: the first item 1/11 deadline is today, so this year's rush has passed. The RCR covered three years (2023-2026), so it is not yearly. Lawyers' RCR was due 31 Jul, not 30 Jun. I found no tool that builds tailored RMCPs. Two risks remain: the FIC distrusts generic templates, and DocFox/LSSA is entrenched with attorneys. FIC registrations total about 55k institutions.
